correctness.rationale: A permanent k-pebble strategy preserves coordinatewise equality partitions for fixed dimension whenever both alphabets have at least k symbols; k-1 survivors leave a fresh symbol in each coordinate. This preserves equality and Hamming-distance-one adjacency for any quantifier depth. If alphabet sizes below k match, there is an isomorphism. Three-variable distance recursion separates every unequal dimension; a clique on at most k vertices separates unequal truncated alphabets. For k=1 all diagonal atoms agree and structures are nonempty. For k=2, the three possible pair patterns are matchable indefinitely in all dimensions at least two, and a nonedge sentence distinguishes complete graphs from noncomplete ones. Each implication, boundary and the dimension-independent relative width q+1 follows from these facts. Fourteen finite orbit-game comparisons matched the predictions but were not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The object H(d,q) is the canonical family of Cartesian powers of complete graphs, with dimensions and alphabets of arbitrary size. The result is a complete natural infinite classification for all fixed-variable widths, including the exceptional one- and two-variable theories, arbitrary-dimensional visibility by three variables, sharp truncation of alphabet information, canonical least representatives, and a relative distinguishing width q+1 independent of dimension. Though the d=2 square rook case is previously covered and is not claimed new, the arbitrary-dimensional two-parameter classification and its sharp dimension/size contrast form a motivated structural whole rather than an arbitrary finite slice or a mere numerical recomputation.
